sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Bodies**: Institutions created by an Act of Parliament (e.g., NGT, CPCB). They possess legal authority and defined powers under specific legislation.
• **Executive/Advisory Bodies**: Created via government resolution (e.g., National Board for Wildlife - NBWL). They lack independent legislative power but influence policy.
• **Constitutional Mandate**: Article 48A (State's duty to protect environment) and Article 51A(g) (Fundamental duty of citizens) form the bedrock of these institutions.
• **Key Metric**: The 'Polluter Pays Principle' and 'Precautionary Principle' are the guiding judicial doctrines for these institutions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **E-Waste Management**: CPCB monitors compliance under E-Waste (Management) Rules.
• **Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ)**: Managed by NCZMA (National Coastal Zone Management Authority) under EPA, 1986.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Manpower shortage in State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs), lack of scientific data, and political interference.
• **Solutions**: Digitization of compliance, strengthening 'Green Tribunals', and decentralization to local bodies.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'W-A-T-E-R' (Wildlife, Air, Trees, Environment, Rivers).
• **Decoded Meaning**: W (Wildlife Protection Act 1972), A (Air Act 1981), T (The Environment Protection Act 1986), E (Environment Impact Assessment), R (River Boards Act 1956).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The 'National Ganga Council' is chaired by the Prime Minister, not the Minister of Jal Shakti. Always verify the Chairperson of high-level environmental committees.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Institutional Pluralism' to describe the overlapping roles of MoEFCC, CPCB, and NGT in environmental governance.

keyTakeaways: Distinguish clearly between Statutory (Act-based) and Executive (Resolution-based) bodies.
NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but is guided by principles of natural justice.
The Prime Minister chairs the NBWL and the National Ganga Council.
